Line 150 re-fetches `origin/stable` (updating `refs/remotes/origin/stable`). Line 155 creates the version tag pointing at `origin/stable` (the potentially-updated ref). Line 158 compares `VERSION_TAG^{commit}` against `RELEASE_CHECK_HEAD` — if `origin/stable` moved between the two fetches, the tag points at the new commit, the check fails, and the script exits 7 with "No tag was pushed."”

  PROBLEM: The octopus merge check flags every octopus merge touching a protected path, including clean merges that merely bring in a protected change from a parent.
  WHY: A clean octopus merge may have no merged PR of its own, causing the release check to block a legitimate release even though the parent change was already checked and authorized.

  PROBLEM: `protected_merge_commits` silently returns an empty list when the running Git does not recognize `--remerge-diff`, rather than reporting that Git is older than the required version.
  WHY: An older runner can miss protected merge edits; the suggested guard would raise `ReadError` for Git versions below 2.36.

  WHY: Add an explicit `_git(["--version"], git_dir)` parse guard that raises `ReadError` when git < 2.36, so an older runner fails closed with a clear message instead of missing protected merge edits. (Note: also document the requirement in `check_release`'s docstring.)

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:150-168 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Race condition between fetching origin/stable (line 150) and pushing tags (line 168). If origin/stable advances after the second fetch but before the push, the script force-pushes an older commit, rolling back the remote stable tag.
  WHY: Two concurrent mark-stable.sh invocations can race: operator A fetches origin/stable at commit X, runs the release check, creates a version tag at X. Operator B then advances origin/stable to commit Y and completes their release. Operator A's check at line 158 passes (version tag == RELEASE_CHECK_HEAD == X), but the force-push at line 168 rolls back stable from Y to X. The release check passed for X, but the remote stable moved to Y in between.
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:150-168 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: No synchronization or re-verification immediately before the force-push. The script verifies the local version tag against RELEASE_CHECK_HEAD (line 158), but does not re-fetch origin/stable to confirm the remote tag has not advanced since the second fetch at line 150.
  WHY: The 18-line gap between the second fetch (line 150) and the force-push (line 168) is a race window. A concurrent release can advance origin/stable in that window. The script then pushes an older commit, overwriting the newer stable tag. This is a manual operator script, so concurrent invocations are rare but possible (e.g., recovery scenarios, parallel releases for different major versions).
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:479-480
  PROBLEM: The docstring at line 467-468 states an octopus merge "counts when it differs on a protected path from every parent." The code does not implement that check. It runs `git rev-list --min-parents=3 <range> -- <protected pathspecs>`, which lists every octopus merge that touches a protected path, including clean octopus merges that merely bring in a protected change from one parent.
  WHY: A clean octopus merge has no merged PR of its own (merges are created by `git merge`, not PRs), so `commits/{sha}/pulls` returns an empty list and it is blocked with "no merged pull request carries this commit" — a false positive that blocks a legitimate release even though the parent commit that introduced the change was already checked and authorized separately.
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:479
  PROBLEM: The octopus merge check lists all octopus merges touching a protected path rather than only those that differ from every parent, contradicting the docstring and risking false-positive release blocks.
  WHY: Replace the bare `rev-list --min-parents=3` with a per-commit check that compares the merge's tree against each parent for protected paths — e.g., use `git diff-tree -c --name-only <sha> -- <pathspecs>` and only include the SHA when every parent differs on a protected path. Alternatively, document that octopus merges are listed unconditionally as a conservative fail-closed behavior and update the docstring to match. (2 related items)
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
